- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.5), model frequently overestimates downward trend — adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion when sentiment is volatile — add 1–3% buffer to forecast if recent 5-day avg is > 70.0.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment swings >0.5 in last 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “recovery” patterns (e.g., 2+ negative days followed by positive), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast by 2–4% for next 5 days.
